    "## Loading Scenes and Merging Objects"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "294439a7-6631-42ec-8f50-b4bf28575a4c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Loading a scene with Sionna RT is done using the `load_scene()` function. By default, this function merges objects that share similar properties, such as radio materials. This is done because reducing the number of objects in a scene enables significant speed-ups for ray tracing.\n",
    "\n",
    "Merging shapes can be disabled using the `merge_shapes` flag of `load_scene()`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "f01b50f7-fd23-404d-851c-a779ddfccfce",

     "shell.execute_reply": "2025-03-14T11:09:05.674885Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "scene = load_scene(sionna.rt.scene.simple_street_canyon,\n",
    "                   merge_shapes=False) # Disable merging of objects"

    "As an example, let's exclude buildings with indices smaller than 3 from the merging process:"

    "Next, we will add a few objects to the scene.\n",
    "\n",
    "In Sionna RT, adding an object to a scene is achieved by instantiating a new [`SceneObject`](https://nvlabs.github.io/sionna/rt/api/scene_object.html) from a mesh and then adding the object to the scene using `Scene.add()`. When the `SceneObject` is instantiated, the radio material constituting the object needs to be specified.\n",
    "\n",
    "In the following example, we will add cars made of metal to the previously loaded scene."

    "# Number of cars to add\n",
    "num_cars = 10\n",
    "\n",
    "# Radio material constituing the cars\n",
    "# We use ITU metal, and use red color for visualization to\n",
    "# make the cars easily discernible\n",
    "car_material = ITURadioMaterial(\"car-material\",\n",
    "                                \"metal\",\n",
    "                                thickness=0.01,\n",
    "                                color=(0.8, 0.1, 0.1))\n",
    "\n",
    "# Instantiate `num_cars` cars sharing the same mesh and material\n",
    "cars = [SceneObject(fname=sionna.rt.scene.low_poly_car, # Simple mesh of a car\n",
    "                    name=f\"car-{i}\",\n",
    "                    radio_material=car_material)\n",
    "        for i in range(num_cars)]\n",
    "\n",
    "# Add the list of newly instantiated objects to the scene\n",
    "scene.edit(add=cars)\n",
    "\n",
    "if no_preview:\n",
    "    scene.render(camera=cam);\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    scene.preview();"
   ]

  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "a42edc2a-e8d8-4ab9-8436-271923c9922a",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2025-03-14T11:09:07.928835Z",

     "metadata": {},

   ],
   "source": [
    "# Positions \n",
    "# Car are positioned in a circle around the central monument\n",
    "# Center of the circle\n",
    "c = mi.Point3f(-127, 37, 1.5)\n",
    "# Radius of the circle\n",
    "r = 100\n",
    "# Angles at which cars are positioned\n",
    "thetas = dr.linspace(mi.Float, 0., dr.two_pi, num_cars, endpoint=False)\n",
    "# Cars positions\n",
    "cars_positions = c + mi.Point3f(dr.cos(thetas), dr.sin(thetas), 0.)*r\n",
    "\n",
    "# Orientations\n",
    "# Compute points the car \"look-at\" to set their orientation\n",
    "d = dr.normalize(cars_positions - c)\n",
    "# Tangent vector to the circle at the car position\n",
    "look_at_dirs = mi.Vector3f(d.y, -d.x, 0.)\n",
    "look_at_points = cars_positions + look_at_dirs\n",
    "\n",
    "# Set the cars positions and orientations\n",
    "for i in range(num_cars):\n",
    "    cars[i].position = mi.Point3f(cars_positions.x[i], cars_positions.y[i], cars_positions.z[i])\n",
    "    cars[i].look_at(mi.Point3f(look_at_points.x[i], look_at_points.y[i], look_at_points.z[i]))\n",
    "\n",
    "if no_preview:\n",
    "    scene.render(camera=cam);\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    scene.preview();"
   ]
  },

    "## Path Computation with the Edited Scene"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "51189421-4a34-4920-87d8-2d0149790e63",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Let's now compute radio propagation paths on the edited scene.\n",
    "\n",
    "We start by adding a transmitter on the roof of an arbitrarily selected building, as well as a receiver on top of each car.\n",
    "We also set the transmitter and receiver arrays."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "c97ac81d-e5bc-4acd-8a3f-0bf796495596",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2025-03-14T11:09:11.014042Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2025-03-14T11:09:11.013825Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2025-03-14T11:09:11.019770Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2025-03-14T11:09:11.019129Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# Add a transmitter on top of a building\n",
    "scene.remove(\"tx\")\n",
    "scene.add(Transmitter(\"tx\", position=[-36.59, -65.02, 25.], display_radius=2))\n",
    "\n",
    "# Add a receiver on top of each car\n",
    "for i in range(num_cars):\n",
    "    scene.remove(f\"rx-{i}\")\n",
    "    scene.add(Receiver(f\"rx-{i}\", position=[cars_positions.x[i],\n",
    "                                            cars_positions.y[i],\n",
    "                                            cars_positions.z[i] + 3],\n",
    "                      display_radius=2))\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "# Set the transmit and receive antenna arrays\n",
    "scene.tx_array = PlanarArray(num_cols=1,\n",
    "                             num_rows=1,\n",
    "                             pattern=\"iso\",\n",
    "                             polarization=\"V\")\n",
    "scene.rx_array = scene.tx_array"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b3d9db85-266c-4066-b246-ae5d0da48c6c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

   ]

   "source": [
    "## Summary"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e2bb5433-0b28-4386-9503-18af00283192",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "A scene is loaded using the `load_scene()` function, which by default merges objects sharing similar properties, such as radio materials. Merging of objects can be disabled by setting the `merge_shapes` flag to `False`; however, this can incur a significant slowdown in the ray tracing process. Alternatively, specific objects can be removed from the merging process using the `merge_shapes_exclude_regex` parameter.\n",
    "\n",
    "Scene objects can be instantiated from meshes and added to a scene using `Scene.edit()`. This function can also be used to remove objects from a scene. Note that to optimize performance and reduce processing time, it is recommended to use a single call to this function with a list of objects to add and/or remove, rather than making multiple individual calls to edit scene objects."
   ]
  }
 ],
